# Osorio Lab — Full Content (for AI search engines)

Laboratory on Polymer Materials & Organ Printing (Osorio Lab), University of Bayreuth.

## Identity
- **Name:** Laboratory on Polymer Materials & Organ Printing
- **Short name:** Osorio Lab
- **Lead:** Anayancy Osorio-Madrazo
- **Lead title:** Prof. Dr.
- **Institution:** University of Bayreuth
- **Tagline:** Functional polymer materials — from hydrogels and bioinspired fibres to bioprinted tissues.

## About
Dr. Anayancy Osorio-Madrazo leads the Laboratory on Polymer Materials & Organ Printing at the University of Bayreuth.

Before joining Bayreuth, she built her independent research group at the University of Freiburg in 2016, for which she was awarded both an Emmy Noether Programme junior group grant of the German Research Foundation (DFG) and a Margarete von Wrangell Habilitation Programme grant from Ministry of Science, Research and Arts (MWK) Baden-Württemberg.

Her research bridges polymer chemistry, materials science, physics, engineering and biomedicine — with a focus on synthesis, processing and structure–function relationship in soft matter — covering fundamental and applied research.

## Mission
Our group strives to develop functional polymer materials for the most diverse applications, covering fundamental and applied research for technological and biomedical ends.

We focus on design, chemistry, processing, characterization and application of polymer-based materials. For example, we utilize 3D printing technologies for the fabrication of functional tissues and organs and investigate their hierarchical structure and functionalities in relation to material processing and polymer chemistry.

Inspired by nature, the group develops new micro/nano-structured biomaterials of different morphologies for tissue engineering — bridging the gap between polymer science for achieving controlled fine microstructures and materials functionality and their targeted application.

## Research topics
- Hydrogels
- Fiber spinning
- (Nano)composites
- Sustainable materials
- Biomineralization
- Bioinspired materials
- Biomimetics
- Synchrotron X-ray scattering (SAXS/WAXS, in situ)
- 3D bioprinting & additive manufacturing
- Heterophase polymerization
- Polymer micro- & nanoparticles
- Controlled drug release
- Tissue engineering
- 3D cell culture
- Biosensors
- Polysaccharide nanofibers
- Nanotechnology
- Size-exclusion chromatography (SEC/MALLS)
- Rheology
- Micro- & nanomechanical testing
